display.title: Parshas Chayei Sarah: Eliezer at the Well and Giving More Than Asked
display.summary_short: How we live with the weekly parsha day by day, and the lesson of kindness from Eliezer's search for a wife for Yitzchak: give even more than you are asked.
display.summary_long: A parsha talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for the week of Parshas Chayei Sarah. Uncle Yossi explains that the weekly parsha is divided into seven portions, one for each day, so that from Sunday to Shabbos our whole week is filled with its learning, just as the Alter Rebbe taught us to 'live with the times'. He then turns to chapter 24, verse 14: Eliezer, Avraham's faithful servant, prayed for a sign that the girl who offered water not only to him but also to his camels was the right wife for Yitzchak. Since Avraham was a man of kindness, Yitzchak's wife had to excel in kindness too, giving more than she was asked. Children can follow this example by sharing what they have with friends, and the mitzvah missions of Tzivos Hashem are full of such good deeds.
display.lesson: Practice kindness by giving and sharing even more than others ask of you.
